claims.evidence: https://osf.io/download/6a216eefee84266e775b8113/ section 2.3 (p.7) and Table 3 (p.8); likelihood-only row. Pinned E3_analysis.R contains the corresponding executable lmer/AIC expression at lines 239-240; the source uses the same formula.
claims.rationale: The original article prints approximately 1722, whereas the source obtains 1766.298 from the original model predictions and AIC procedure. This is separate from the later RMSE-versus-MAE robustness comparison. Pilot diagnostics explain the discrepancy: R parses (t/(t+f)) as terms t and t:f. Protecting the arithmetic with I() gives AIC 1721.98145543401; the Sol pilot independently gets 1721.9814554340073 using the precomputed Proportion variable and documented mixed-effects option. Both diagnostics change how the predictor is specified relative to the executable nested expression and are non-scoring.

notes.claim_list: The five numerical AIC targets occur in the Experiment 3 Results paragraph following Figure 8 (p.1021), with approximation symbols. They are not exact readings from the Figure 8 fixed-effects bars. The source report Table 3 supplies mixed-effects AICs: C1/C2 have executable lmer expressions in the pinned script; C3-C5 use its documented mixed-effects option, instantiated by the reproducer.
notes.sol: C1-C5 target the printed numerical heuristic-comparison paragraph on p.1021, not values extracted from the Figure 8 fixed-effects bars. The paper describes Figure 8 as fixed effects but the source Table 3 reports mixed-effects values. C1/C2 are executable lmer expressions in the pinned script. C3-C5 follow the authors' explicit mixed-effects instruction (add participant/item random intercepts and use lmer), instantiated by the reproducer; their references are scoped to that documented intended procedure, not the default lm/dredge branch. No equivalence of fixed- and mixed-effects models is asserted. The 1722-versus-1766.298 difference remains a P2 discrepancy in the shipped heuristic expression. No RMSE/MAE robustness specification supplies these references. v1.1 adds both pilot explanations for C1 as explicitly non-scoring diagnostics. They converge on an arithmetic-proportion mixed model; merely switching between fixed and mixed effects does not itself establish the shipped expression is correct. No C1 status, severity, or scoring-reference change is made.
notes.claude: No paper alternative under R7. The exhibit now points to the Results paragraph after Fig. 8; references follow the authors' documented mixed-effects procedure. Reconciled with the second labeller (see reconciliation.md). The final judgement is the structured label; notes_blind_original keeps the pre-reconciliation blind notes, which are historical and superseded wherever they conflict with the final label.
notes.claude_blind_original_historical: Claim list: the exhibit is given as 'Figure 6', but in the published paper the Experiment 3 AIC comparison is Fig. 8 (p. 1021). Provenance: the shipped E3_analysis.R (SHA matches pin) computes fixed-effects lm AICs for Bayes/UPCO/Competence via MuMIn::dredge, with a comment saying to switch to lmer with (1|lab)+(1|Subject) for the mixed models. Prior-only and proportion AICs are computed with lmer at lines 239-240. The report's Table 3 values for Bayes/UPCO/Competence (410.086/497.267/506.928) come from lmer models the reproducer added (E3_analysis_FD.R on https://osf.io/uyrq8/), following that comment. The report says this AIC table (supplementary Figure 12) 'was not included in the provided code'. So C3-C5 match only via a trivial reproducer addition. The paper is also internally inconsistent here: it says Fig. 8's AICs are fixed-effects estimates, yet the printed values coincide with the mixed-model numbers. C1 severity: I chose P2 rather than P1 because it is a baseline heuristic comparison and the ranking and conclusion are unchanged. P1 is arguable, since beating the heuristics is a stated Exp 3 hypothesis. My own hypothesis, not the report's: inside an R formula, t/(t+f) is nesting syntax, not a proportion (no I()). That could explain why the code's value differs from whatever produced 1722. The report's headline is that results 'reproduce almost perfectly'. Some scripts (E1, parts of E3 after the AIC section) needed minor fixes to run. Hence 'computationally reproducible' is an acceptable alternative.
